question: Which Indian state has become the first to establish a commission dedicated to the rights and welfare of senior citizens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Kerala has become the first Indian state to pass a law creating a Senior Citizens Commission to ensure the rights, welfare, and rehabilitation of the elderly.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kerala State Senior Citizens Commission Bill was passed on 19 March 2025.**
 
• Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan announced the formation of this first-of-its-kind commission in India.
 
• The commission will focus on rehabilitation, welfare, security, and active societal participation of senior citizens.
 
• It will also address hardships such as neglect, exploitation, and loneliness faced by the elderly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kerala**__ consistently ranks among the top Indian states in terms of elderly welfare and healthcare indicators.
 
• __**Senior Citizens Commission**__ will issue guidelines and implement policies to support and engage senior citizens in the development of "New Kerala."
 
• This initiative reinforces the objectives of inclusive governance and social justice, promoting dignity and care for all age groups.
 
• The commission is part of Kerala’s broader efforts under the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government to ensure dignified ageing and community integration.
